newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc hits lowest levels vs dlr since Feb 95.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc hits lowest levels vs dlr since Feb 95.

text.p: The Swiss franc fell sharply versus the dollar, dipping back to levels unseen versus the U.S. unit since February 1995, traders said.

The dollar rose to as high as 1.2777 Swiss francs in afternoon trade following release of U.S. October non-farm payrolls. It was the highest level for dollar/Swiss since it traded above 1.2800 francs in mid-February 1995.
"The main reason (for the Swiss franc's drop versus the dollar) is that it has broken sharply versus the mark," said Adam Beudin, trading strategist at Credit Suisse.
He said the Swiss franc's recent drop against the mark had played a big part in undermining the Swiss currency's strength against the dollar.
The mark rose to a high Friday of 83.90 Swiss centimes, which also put it back at levels unseen in nearly two years.
The latest move in mark/Swiss "has got people scared we have entered a new stage of Swiss franc weakness," Beudin said.
He said the mark now appeared to have scope to rise to 85.00 Swiss centimes.
Activity was busy on Friday afternoon despite closure of some European centres due to the All Saint's Day holiday.
"There is a lot going through, and the franc has weakened," said Freddy Lutz, in charge of currency trading at Bank Julius Baer.
He believed the mark had room for further gains back to perhaps the 85.00 to 90.00 centime area in the next two months.

Current levels have brought mark/Swiss closer to an area which is seen as a more characteristic range. Mark/Swiss fell sharply in mid-1995 as funds flowed out of Germany on nervousness tied to worries about European economic and monetary union.
